USGS 07289000 returned no recent gage height; no extension.

USGS lists at least six gauge sites at Vicksburg since 1871, all on the same datum but on a sloping water surface; in 1927 the Corps canal gauge read about 2 ft above the bridge gauge. The median level drops about 10 ft from the 1920s to the 1930s and 1940s; site changes and channel changes may both play a part, and the file does not say which gauge each year uses.
Gauge zero 46.23 ft NGVD29 per the CWMS MVK location record (USGS 07289000 lists 46.22 ft NGVD29).
Levels are rounded to 0.01 ft: the API converts from stored meters and returns float noise such as 12.979999999999999.

measurement_history.fact: Mississippi River Commission staff gauge at the mouth of the Yazoo diversion canal, 1.5 miles above the bridge, used Dec. 1871 to Sept. 1929.
Weather Bureau staff gauge half a mile upstream of the bridge site, used May 1873 to Oct. 1919.
Weather Bureau gauge moved to the mouth of the Yazoo canal, then to an inclined gauge on the canal from Dec. 1, 1922 to Aug. 31, 1934.
Weather Bureau readings moved to a wire-weight gauge at the Vicksburg bridge; nonrecording until Dec. 31, 1962.
Water-stage recorder on the left bank near the bridge, 1963 to 1967.
Gauge moved 1.1 miles upstream for 1968 to 1976.
Gauge moved to the left bank at the downstream side of the Interstate 20 bridge, its present site.
USGS: all these gauges use the same datum, but readings differ because the water surface slopes between them.
The 1927 crest read 58.4 ft on the Corps canal gauge and about 56.0 ft on the USGS bridge gauge.
Gauge zero 46.225 ft above 1929 datum (1941 adjustment, Corps bench mark), or 46.16 ft above mean Gulf level.
USACE lists gauge zero as 46.23 ft NGVD29; NWS lists no datum for this gauge.

public_notes: The Vicksburg record joins readings from at least six gauge locations, all set to the same gauge zero but on a sloping river, so the same water can read differently from one site to the next. In 1927 the canal gauge read about 2 feet higher than the bridge gauge; the Army Corps file does not say which gauge it used in each year.
